title: Advisor
intro: A second, stronger model the main model consults at decision points. Each rule has a stable id; turn one off with `forge advisor rule off <id>` (per repo, or --global), then `forge sync`.

rules.text: Before committing to an approach on a multi-step task, consult the advisor and apply its guidance before editing.
rules.rationale: Plan quality decides the outcome of a long task while most of its turns are routine. One consultation before the first edit is cheaper than a wrong plan carried through every later turn.

rules.text: When the same error recurs after two attempts, stop and consult the advisor before trying again.
rules.rationale: A recurring failure means the diagnosis is wrong, not the patch. A fresh read of the whole transcript by a stronger model finds the cause; a third patch on the same diagnosis rarely does.

rules.text: Before declaring a task complete, consult the advisor for an independent check of the result against the request.
rules.rationale: The model that did the work is the worst judge of what it missed. An independent reviewer that sees the full conversation catches the dropped requirement and the untested path.

rules.text: Consult the advisor before changing code that handles money, auth, secrets, migrations or security.
rules.rationale: Mistakes there are expensive and often silent in tests. A second opinion at the decision point costs one advisor call; a double-charge race or an auth bypass costs far more.

rules.text: When the advisor's guidance contradicts what the files or a failed step show, surface the conflict instead of following the guidance blindly.
rules.rationale: The advisor reads the transcript, not the repository. Where its claim and the evidence disagree, the evidence is the fact and the disagreement is the finding to report.

rules.text: Do not consult the advisor on short, well-specified tasks: every call re-reads the whole conversation at the advisor's rate and its own read is never cached.
rules.rationale: The advisor adds little on a task with nothing to plan, and its full-transcript read is billed on every call. The three moments above are where it pays for itself.

ranking.note: Claude Code ranks models by capability for the advisor role; an advisor must rank at or above the session's main model. Rows are the models the pairing table names, lowest rank first; the Mythos rows mirror the API's compatibility table (Mythos and Fable of one version rank equal). A family alias (sonnet, opus, fable) stands for that family's newest row. Haiku can call the advisor but never act as one.
